target_moa.text: Bexagliflozin is a sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor; SGLT2 is the predominant transporter responsible for reabsorption of glucose from the glomerular filtrate; by inhibiting SGLT2, bexagliflozin reduces renal reabsorption of filtered glucose and lowers the renal threshold for glucose, producing glucosuria.

citations.quote: Bexagliflozin is a small molecule inhibitor of the sodium-glucose linked transporter 2 (sodium-glucose co-transporter-2, SGLT2), the transporter responsible for reabsorption of the majority of glucose from the renal glomerular filtrate in the renal proximal tubule. Bexagliflozin is a small molecule inhibitor of the sodium-glucose linked transporter 2 (sodium-glucose co-transporter-2, SGLT2), the transporter responsible for reabsorption of the majority of glucose from the renal glomerular filtrate in the renal proximal tubule.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >5%): female genital mycotic infections, urinary tract infection, and increased urination. In the placebo-controlled pool (Placebo N=300, BRENZAVVY N=372): increased urination 7% vs 3%, urinary tract infection 6% vs 4%, female genital mycotic infections 6% vs 0%. Serious risks consistent with the SGLT2 inhibitor class include ketoacidosis, urosepsis and pyelonephritis.

summary.text: Standard review NDA (214373) received 10/22/2021 with a PDUFA goal date of 1/22/2023; approved as a fifth-in-class SGLT2 inhibitor based on six phase 3 adequate and well-controlled trials, without accelerated approval or expedited-program designations, and without an advisory committee meeting.

citations.quote:
Priority or standard	Standard
Submit date(s)	10/22/2021
Received date(s)	10/22/2021
PDUFA goal date	1/22/2023

Six adequate and well-controlled phase 3 trials conducted in subjects with T2DM provide substantial evidence of effectiveness for the pursued glycemic control indication (Trials C-419, C-423, C-448, C-450, C-476, and C-480; Table 3).

There was no advisory committee meeting conducted for this application. Although bexagliflozin is an NME, the efficacy endpoint (HbA1c) was straightforward and well accepted, and there were no controversial efficacy or safety issues with this fifth-in-class product that would have benefitted from an advisory committee meeting.
